items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: Interviewer mentions: '...everybody from Dolly Parton to Tom Scott.' Interviewee does not respond with any personal anecdote or confirmation of a direct relationship with Dolly Parton.

ctx.x: wanted to see Bobby. And we were doing an R&B band, it was a wonderful R&B band and we were opening for him and we were rehearsing. And it was after they did their sound check and they took their break and we were rehearsing and he told Sal Nestico he says, “I want you to hear this kid.” So they didn’t leave, they went up and they sat all the way up in the very top of the venue to listen to me play. And Shew, Bobby and I, we’re like brothers, real brothers. And next thing you know I get a call to fly to New York…

That’s a fascinating backstory to all that. I want to take you back to your busy studio life. I came across one of those on-line Chuck Findley discographies, you know, the never- ending scroll. And I started to count, literally, and I said this is not going to work. But what I did see is that in 1979, according to this list, you played on 26 LPs. Like that’s more than two a month and everybody from Dolly Parton to Tom Scott. So I don’t have a question, it’s simply an observation. But I wonder if you can describe,…

Well that was wonderful actually. Well it was not really nice, I mean John Audino had passed away and I was in Germany. I was doing a little tour with Peter Herbolzheimer in Germany. And I was considering actually moving there because our son was young and I wanted him to get the culture and learn other languages other than just English. I wanted him to learn German and go to schools there. They know three or four languages everybody over there. They speak and you feel like a fool when I went over there the first…
